title: The Rowdy Queen
text: “Queen-sama! We’re the victims here! Some nonsensical person calling herself Blazer Milly just up and attacked us, calling us bandits! That woman’s gotta be one of the Shield Devil’s cronies, no doubt about it!”
Believe me! — and with that, the man launched into some self-serving excuse, indeed.
“Why does it always end up being Iwatani-sama’s fault around here, I wonder?”

“Isn’t it just that people figure if they blame every bad thing in this country on Shield Hero, it’ll stick? Like… they bring up some old grudge, issue some unreasonable order, and when you push back they go ‘You haven’t reflected at all!’ or ‘The past grudge never fades!’ — thinking that gives them the moral high ground. Even when the person saying it wasn’t even born during whatever grudge they’re on about.”
Haaah… Father sighed, indeed. There sure were a lot of people like that. That said, outside of this particular loop, pinning things on Father had become rather rare.
“Silence!”
The Queen barked at the captured bandits, indeed. But the bandits weren’t backing down, no.
“If you’re so sure we’re villains, then drag that Blazer Milly person out here!”
Isn’t she standing right in front of you? Should I be the one to point that out, I wonder?
“Quite the performance… or is there some kind of script for these bandits in this footage? Didn’t they hear Blazer Milly’s lines at all?”
“It’s the Melromarc Rise-Up, indeed.”
“That’s not it. It’s a mix of several things.”
Oh? Was that so, I wonder?
“A nonsensical person, you say… If you want to see her that badly, I’ll show you!”

Bam! The Queen snapped her fan shut, then whipped out a compact and — yes, transformed right there too, indeed. With a flash, the transformation finished, and she looked down upon the bandits, indeed.

“Don’t you dare tell me you’ve forgotten my face! The very flower of evil I showed you all so clearly back then! Did you truly think I, the ruler of this nation, wouldn’t recognize what I had cut down myself?”
“T-that can’t be!? That nonsensical woman is the Queen!?”
The bandits, struck speechless, went pale and crumbled to their knees, indeed.
“Do you still intend to play innocent after this?”
“D-damn it…”
With the very hero they’d captured now passing judgment right before their eyes, there was no room left to feign ignorance — more like, there was simply no escape at all, indeed.
“Somehow I feel like she could even put corrupt nobles on trial with this.”
“There’s footage of that too, you know? Want to see it?”
“No… I’d rather not.”
Father declined the vision crystal Rafumi held out, indeed.
“Between Melromarc and Shieldfreeden, which is less painful to watch…”
“Please don’t weigh that on a scale.”
Rabbit Guy protested against Father’s dilemma, indeed.
“Why not just watch both?”
“Ren, no thanks.”

“I get roped into playing that weird judge role too, you know? Ren, don’t play innocent, playing one of the guys Rafumi caught who shouts ‘Don’t think that just because you’re heroes you can judge us!’ I’m the real deal and I still get called ‘a judge who looks remarkably like him.’”

“You have my sympathy there. But still… essentially passing judgment on villains you captured yourself… and somehow they threw in a cherry-blossom tattoo and a rowdy general type into the mix. Is that supposed to feel fresh in some way…?”
Hmm. Father groaned as if lamenting, indeed.
“Whatever the case, I suppose this is the result of the Rowdy Queen-sama’s journey of setting the world right spreading far and wide…”
“Well put, Naofumi…”
“I suppose it’s a necessary evil to stop the decline in public order…”

Though I don’t want to imitate it myself, Father added. Either way, it seemed this was how Father and the others managed to guess the reason behind Fiancée’s running away from home. All sorts of things happened after that too, but in the end, the fighting continued on, largely peacefully, all the way up to the wave that marked the finale. The decline in Melromarc’s public order, thanks largely to the efforts of Ren, the Queen, and even Trash, settled down considerably once capable talent had been cultivated. The same held true for Shieldfreeden, where Itsuki had been active. And yet, what stood out was that both Itsuki and the Queen kept up their activities even after the waves ended, declaring that the fight continues regardless. That was how, impressively, the days went on passing by, indeed.
“So this is…”

I found myself standing in a space I recognized from before, indeed. A strange place where, despite the darkness, only I seemed to be glowing. I understood well enough, in some vague way, that this loop had come to an end. Then, gliding in from nowhere in particular, the spear spirit wearing Rival’s form appeared, indeed.
“Do you intend to show up in that form again, I say!”
It seemed Rival couldn’t come here herself. In that sense, I had the upper hand, indeed. And yet, savoring that sense of superiority felt distasteful with this particular opponent, indeed.
“Oh? You remembered, huh. Once you recognize something, understanding comes quick, I suppose.”
With a shift, the spear spirit reverted to its original form — something like a clump of light, indeed.
“I never forgot in the first place, I say!”
“Well, you had already recognized it by the time this loop began, so I suppose it’s no wonder.”
Just then… something caught my eye — far off in the distance, what looked like several points of light shimmering. What could that be, I wonder?
“Ah, curious about that?”
“What is it, I say?”
“That’s, well… it’s the spirits who took a liking to this particular loop, fighting over who gets to take charge of it… no, wait, ‘discussing’ is more accurate.”
“You corrected yourself just now, indeed.”

“There’s a bit of an ugly squabble involved too, if I’m honest… well, shake things up a little and this world turned out to be quite the appealing deal from a spirit’s perspective, that’s the reason.”
So apparently, from the spirits’ point of view, this particular loop had turned out to be an extremely good deal, indeed.
“That’s because of how wild Rafumi went rampaging about, I say.”
“No, that’s got nothing to do with it.”
“That one rampaged way too much, I say.”
“I won’t deny it, but I think it’s a minor factor in the grand scheme.”
“You call that minor, I say!?”
That was rampaging at its finest, indeed!
“Then it must be the noisy tug-of-war caused by the claw spirit’s cheating habits, I say.”
Constantly swapping owners like that is far too much. Filo-tan should just commit to one, I say!
“That’s got absolutely nothing to do with it — or rather, don’t go forcing out random accusations. You’re not the old you anymore, so please stop picking fights out of nowhere.”

“So then, Ren gets enshrined as a hero after Kuro-chan’s own taste, becomes King of Melromarc, and the Queen turns into a Blazer warrior — and that loop is somehow the one the spirits found most agreeable, I say?”
Those spirits sure had peculiar tastes, indeed.
“No, no… I’d appreciate it if you didn’t say things that could be misunderstood, unlike the sword spirit maybe. It has absolutely nothing to do with it.”

The spear spirit shot that down smoothly, as if implicitly admitting that the sword spirit did indeed have a taste for Rafumi’s antics disguised as Ren. Come to think of it, Ren’s swordplay always seemed particularly sharp whenever he was off playing around with Kuro-chan, indeed.
“Then perhaps the spirits favor the loop involving the slave trade, I say?”

“Is it really a good idea for you all to go charging so eagerly toward morally dicey topics like that? Well, brushing off sparks that fall on you, villainy or not, I can overlook to some extent since it’s at least somewhat justifiable in conscience — but that’s not it either. Actually, the sun’s going to set at this rate, so let’s just get to the answer, shall we?”
“Then hurry up and say it, I say.”
Every single guess I made turned out wrong, apparently, indeed.
“After doing all sorts of things different from other loops in the one we were just in… how do you still manage to get it wrong?”
The spear spirit muttered complaints under its breath, but I paid it no mind, indeed. As I was thinking that—
“I wonder what anyone could possibly expect from this man…”
Some manner of light drifted over and murmured that, indeed. What was this, I wonder?
“Is it Mole, I say?”

“Not Imiya-chan and the others. Well, I suppose compared to you illustrious seniors, I’m the newest of newcomers… though, being a spirit born from a branching world, it’s a shame my power isn’t all that strong, if I do say so.”
“Something to look forward to in the future, I’d say. Well, you managed to get here thanks to having cultivated quite a bit of spiritual power in your past life, so do your best.”
“I suppose so. Still, a second life — who knows how it’ll turn out.”
What in the world is this thing, I wonder? As I pointed at it, the spear spirit wavered and flared up in a provocative, fiery sort of way, indeed.
“There’s no way this man could understand, is there.”
“What was that, I say!? Are you mocking me, I say!?”
“It’s simply the truth, isn’t it! Honestly, you really never change, not even a little!”

What does this thing even know about me, I wonder!? It’s as if it had been watching everything, indeed! Narrowing my eyes to focus, I made out… a rabbit? Something like that silhouette came into view, indeed.
